action_assessment.summary: Most core activities are represented, but the initial purchase is omitted and treasurer checking is duplicated/misplaced after payment, adding unsupported behavior.

flow_assessment.summary: Required precedence is broken: corrected reports do not reliably return to supervisor review, and an extra treasurer check is placed after payment instead of before it.

control_flow_assessment.summary: Branch continuation and recurrence are wrong: both correction loops are misrouted, approved/accepted processing continues incorrectly through a merge to another treasurer check, and some exits bypass required approval/payment behavior.

result.explanation: The source requires any returned report to go back to the employee for correction and then again to supervisor review before any further treasurer handling; only after treasurer acceptance does payment occur, followed by waiting for confirmation and ending. In the generated graph, the supervisor-rejection loop cycles between rejection and employee resubmission without returning to the supervisor approval decision, the treasurer-return loop cycles back to the treasurer-return action instead of routing back through supervisor review, and a merge sends even the accepted-and-paid path to another treasurer check before termination. These defects change the core rework, approval, and completion behavior of the whole process, not just local labels.
